LESSON: PASSING SPEAKING

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Passing SPEAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Passing SPEAKING. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Convey messages effectively at home and in school.
2. Retell short stories in and out of school.
3. Use relevant vocabulary when engaging in dialogue. encouraged to answer
4. Take pleasure in passing verbal messages and retelling stories in and out of school. activities where they view a video clip and then talk about it in pairs or in small groups. 17 Learners could be encouraged to talk about what they saw in a field trip or nature walk.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Convey messages effectively at home and in school.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to convey messages effectively at home and in school. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Retell short stories in and out of school.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to retell short stories in and out of school. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. Use relevant vocabulary when engaging in dialogue. encouraged to answer
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use relevant vocabulary when engaging in dialogue. encouraged to answer. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. Take pleasure in passing verbal messages and retelling stories in and out of school. activities where they view a video clip and then talk about it in pairs or in small groups. 17 Learners could be encouraged to talk about what they saw in a field trip or nature walk.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to take pleasure in passing verbal messages and retelling stories in and out of school. activities where they view a video clip and then talk about it in pairs or in small groups. 17 Learners could be encouraged to talk about what they saw in a field trip or nature walk. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Passing SPEAKING.
2. Explain Passing SPEAKING to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Passing SPEAKING.
4. Show that you can: Convey messages effectively at home and in school.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Passing SPEAKING. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Passing SPEAKING important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Convey messages effectively at home and in school.
2. Retell short stories in and out of school.
3. Use relevant vocabulary when engaging in dialogue. encouraged to answer
4. Take pleasure in passing verbal messages and retelling stories in and out of school. activities where they view a video clip and then talk about it in pairs or in small groups. 17 Learners could be encouraged to talk about what they saw in a field trip or nature walk.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
